**Conversation Overview**

This conversation was a highly technical research session (Session 55) in an ongoing multi-session computational physics project called LOWDIN, focused on deriving and testing an "ordering clause" — a rule governing the sequential filling of atomic orbitals (n+ℓ ordering) across the periodic table. The person is running a long-running research program that spans many sessions, each of which opens a sealed handoff archive, performs computational work, and produces a new sealed archive for the next session. The work involves a chain of ~107 atoms (Z=2 to Z=108), a scalar-relativistic Hartree-Fock-like solver, and a rigorous prediction-before-computation protocol (designated R 1449) where every numerical claim must be filed with a hash and timestamp before any instrument runs.

The session's central work was correcting a misattribution from Session 54 (registered as F55.2): s54 had claimed "the ordering clause is not derivable from the non-relativistic field," but 5f and 6d both carry n+ℓ=8, meaning the Z=90 reversal between them occurs *within* a shell of equal n+ℓ and cannot reach a clause that orders *by* n+ℓ. Checked across all eleven rows tested at c=1e6 (the non-relativistic limit), n+ℓ of the entrant was unchanged at every one. The corrected finding — that the ordering clause *survives* removal of relativity on an adversarially chosen sample — was written into Deliverable 1 (§0, §6.1, §6.3), with the 19-clause checker (gate 86) still passing. Four additional faults were registered and remedied: F55.1 (a `/tmp` copy broke a gate runner's `dirname`-relative `cd`, causing step 5 of the open to silently not run), F55.3 (a gate omitted a data source and failed closed — correct direction), and F55.4 (the job runner's `--wait` command read a stale receipt from a previous run and reported success without actually polling — found only by the fresh-extract test, not by reasoning).

Substantive computational results included closing F54.3 (the only rung-1 channel at Z=88 was 5f, sixth place, 110 mHa below the decision; 7s/6d reproduced exactly at rung 0 with no rung-1 solve), independently confirming Z=90 bit-for-bit with Z=91 as a new row (fields agree at Z=89 and Z=91, disagree only at Z=90), validating a "screen" at Z=92 to avoid walking 13 redundant rows, and answering the transit-width question owed since Session 47 (transit widths (4f, 5f) = (1,2) with relativity and (1,1) without — the asymmetry is entirely relativistic, with the second proton of 5f transit being the same 183 mHa 6d/5f differential that produces the Z=90 reversal). Four predictions were filed before their instruments ran, all four confirmed by gates scoring 7/7, 9/9, 6/6, and 7/7 respectively, each can-failed in three independent ways. The session closed with a fresh-extract test showing zero-line diff against the reference replay log, and the sealed archive `LOWDIN-HANDOFF-55.tar.gz` was produced. A ruling was requested for Session 56 on whether the adversarial 11-row sample is sufficient to close Clause 3, or whether a full 107-row c=1e6 walk is owed.
